description: Static Type System (M11) - Gradual static typing with full numeric tower (i32, i64, u32, u64, f32, f64), typed/unboxed opcodes for i64/u64/f64, compile-time type checking, typed def/mut/proc, and explicit to conversions.

userStories.title: Value tags, heap types, constructors, accessors, predicates for u32/i64/u64/f64
userStories.description: As a developer, I need runtime value representations for u32, i64, u64, and f64 so that typed computations have concrete value types to operate on.
acceptanceCriteria: Add JACL_TAG_U32 (0x0D) to value.c — unsigned 32-bit integer stored inline in payload (same layout as JACL_TAG_I32 but unsigned)
Add JACL_TAG_I64 (0x0E) to value.c — heap pointer tag for signed 64-bit integer
Add JACL_TAG_U64 (0x0F) to value.c — heap pointer tag for unsigned 64-bit integer
Add JACL_TAG_F64 (0x10) to value.c — heap pointer tag for 64-bit double
Add heap structs: typedef struct { int64_t value; } JaclHeapI64; typedef struct { uint64_t value; } JaclHeapU64; typedef struct { double value; } JaclHeapF64;
Add constructors: jacl_u32(uint32_t) stores inline; jacl_i64(int64_t), jacl_u64(uint64_t), jacl_f64(double) arena-allocate heap struct and store pointer in payload
jacl_i64/jacl_u64/jacl_f64 constructors take arena_t* as first parameter for heap allocation
Add accessors: jacl_as_u32(JaclVal) returns uint32_t; jacl_as_i64(JaclVal) returns int64_t; jacl_as_u64(JaclVal) returns uint64_t; jacl_as_f64(JaclVal) returns double
Add predicates: jacl_is_u32(JaclVal), jacl_is_i64(JaclVal), jacl_is_u64(JaclVal), jacl_is_f64(JaclVal)
All constructors/accessors/predicates follow existing jacl_i32/jacl_f32 patterns with flag propagation
Update test_bytecode.c test_opcode_enum for shifted OP_HALT value if new opcodes are added in this story
Compiles cleanly with -Wall -Wextra -std=c99 -g
All existing tests pass (build.sh)
userStories.notes: u32 is inline (32 bits fit in 56-bit payload). i64/u64/f64 need 64 bits and don't fit in the 56-bit payload, so they use heap pointers. The arena pointer is needed for allocation — follow the same pattern as other heap types (strings, closures). These heap tags are used for boxed representations (dynamic context, collections, globals). In typed/unboxed context, raw 64-bit values live on the VM stack without tags.

userStories.notes: These functions operate on BOXED (tagged) JaclVal values — they extract, compute, re-wrap. They are used by dynamic dispatch (OP_ADD etc.) and as the implementation behind typed opcodes. Follow the exact same pattern as jacl_i32_add and jacl_f32_add in value.c. Add JaclType type field to Local struct (default TYPE_DYN)
Add JaclType type field to Upvalue struct (default TYPE_DYN)

Add helper: bool is_unboxed_type(JaclType t) — true for i64/u64/f64 (types that live raw on VM stack)

userStories.notes: u64 reuses i64 opcodes for add/sub/mul/neg/eq (identical bit patterns in two's complement). Only div/mod/comparisons differ (unsigned semantics). So u64 has 6 unique opcodes, not 11. Total new opcodes: 11 (i64) + 6 (u64) + 11 (f64) + 7 (conversion) + 3 (typed constants) = 38. Type field defaults must be set in compiler__add_local, compiler__add_upvalue, and compiler__set_global_arity (all init type = TYPE_DYN).

userStories.title: VM handlers for i64 and f64 typed opcodes
userStories.description: As a developer, I need VM execution handlers for i64 and f64 typed arithmetic and comparison opcodes so that typed code can run without runtime type dispatch.
acceptanceCriteria: Add VM handlers in vm__run() for all 11 i64 opcodes: OP_ADD_I64 through OP_EQ_I64
i64 handlers operate on raw int64_t stack values: pop two uint64_t, cast to int64_t, compute, push result as uint64_t
OP_ADD_I64: pop b and a as int64_t, push (uint64_t)(a + b)
OP_SUB_I64: pop b and a as int64_t, push (uint64_t)(a - b)
OP_MUL_I64: pop b and a as int64_t, push (uint64_t)(a * b)
OP_DIV_I64: pop b and a as int64_t, if b == 0 set VM error 'division by zero', else push (uint64_t)(a / b)
OP_MOD_I64: pop b and a as int64_t, if b == 0 set VM error, else push (uint64_t)(a % b)
OP_NEG_I64: pop a as int64_t, push (uint64_t)(-a)
OP_LT_I64 through OP_EQ_I64: pop b and a as int64_t, push JACL_TRUE or JACL_FALSE based on comparison
Add VM handlers for all 11 f64 opcodes: OP_ADD_F64 through OP_EQ_F64
f64 handlers: pop uint64_t, memcpy to double (or union-cast), compute, memcpy result back to uint64_t, push
OP_DIV_F64: division by 0.0 sets VM error (consistent with f32 behavior)
OP_MOD_F64: uses fmod(); division by 0.0 sets VM error
f64 comparisons push JACL_TRUE/JACL_FALSE (these are tagged JaclVal booleans, not raw values — comparison results are always boxed bools)
Compiles cleanly with -Wall -Wextra -std=c99 -g
All existing tests pass (build.sh)
userStories.notes: Typed opcodes do NOT check tags — they assume the compiler verified types. Raw i64 values are stored as uint64_t on the stack and reinterpreted as int64_t via cast. Raw f64 values are stored as uint64_t via memcpy/union bit-cast. Division by zero produces a VM runtime error (vm.error_message), not an error-flagged value, since we don't have a tagged value to flag. Comparison results are always JACL_TRUE/JACL_FALSE (tagged booleans) since they may flow into dynamic code (if/while conditions).

userStories.title: VM handlers for u64, conversion, typed constant opcodes, and u32 dynamic dispatch
userStories.description: As a developer, I need the remaining VM handlers (u64 unsigned ops, type conversions, typed constants) and u32 support in existing dynamic dispatch to complete the execution layer.
acceptanceCriteria: Add VM handlers for 6 u64 opcodes: OP_DIV_U64, OP_MOD_U64, OP_LT_U64, OP_GT_U64, OP_LE_U64, OP_GE_U64
u64 handlers: pop as uint64_t (no cast to signed), compute with unsigned semantics, push result
OP_DIV_U64/OP_MOD_U64: check b == 0, VM error if so
Add VM handlers for 7 conversion opcodes: OP_TO_I32, OP_TO_I64, OP_TO_U32, OP_TO_U64, OP_TO_F32, OP_TO_F64, OP_TO_DYN
Each conversion opcode reads a 1-byte source type operand (JaclType enum value) that tells the VM what type the stack value currently is

OP_TO_I64: switch on source type — TYPE_I32: pop tagged JaclVal, extract i32, push (uint64_t)(int64_t)i32; TYPE_U32: extract u32, push zero-extended; TYPE_F64: pop raw double, truncate to int64_t; TYPE_DYN: pop tagged val, runtime extract numeric, convert; etc.

OP_TO_DYN: switch on source type — TYPE_I64: pop raw, arena-alloc JaclHeapI64, push jacl_i64(); TYPE_F64: pop raw, arena-alloc, push jacl_f64(); TYPE_I32: pop raw int32_t, push jacl_i32() (re-tag); similar for u32/u64/f32
OP_TO_DYN needs arena access — use vm->arena or a similar mechanism for heap allocation during execution
Add VM handlers for 3 typed constant opcodes: OP_CONST_I64, OP_CONST_U64, OP_CONST_F64
Typed constant opcodes read a uint16_t index, load raw 8 bytes from the constant pool, push as raw uint64_t (no tag)

Add u32 dispatch cases to existing OP_ADD, OP_SUB, OP_MUL, OP_DIV, OP_MOD, OP_NEG, OP_LT, OP_GT, OP_LE, OP_GE, OP_EQ handlers in vm__run(): after f32 check, add 'else if (jacl_is_u32(a) && jacl_is_u32(b))' calling jacl_u32_* functions
Compiles cleanly with -Wall -Wextra -std=c99 -g
All existing tests pass (build.sh)
userStories.notes: u64 add/sub/mul/neg/eq reuse the i64 opcodes (identical bit patterns in two's complement — the compiler emits OP_ADD_I64 for u64 addition). Only div/mod/comparisons need unsigned-specific opcodes. Conversion opcodes need the source type as an operand byte because the VM doesn't know the type of unboxed stack values. The constant pool needs to support raw 64-bit entries alongside tagged JaclVal entries — either use a separate typed constant array or store raw bytes at indices. OP_TO_DYN requires arena for heap allocation — the VM should have access to the arena used during execution.

userStories.title: Typed def — declare typed immutable bindings with contextual literal typing
userStories.description: As a JACL programmer, I want to declare typed variables with [def TYPE name value] so the compiler tracks types, emits efficient code, and catches type errors.
acceptanceCriteria: Compiler recognizes typed def: [def i64 x 42] — 3 args where first arg is a type keyword

Disambiguation in compiler__compile_command for 'def': if argc == 3 and first arg is AST_LIT_STRING matching a type keyword → typed def (extract type, name is arg 2, value is arg 3). If argc == 2 → untyped def (existing behavior). If argc == 3 and first arg is NOT a type keyword → compile error.
Typed local: compiler stores JaclType in locals[slot].type after adding the local
Typed global: compiler stores JaclType in GlobalArity entry's type field

Contextual literal typing: when compiling the RHS of a typed def, pass the declared type as expected_type context. Integer literals (AST_LIT_INT) in i64 context compile to OP_CONST_I64 with raw int64_t in constant pool. Float literals (AST_LIT_FLOAT) in f64 context compile to OP_CONST_F64 with raw double.
i32/u32/f32 typed def: [def i32 n 42] uses existing tagged constant (OP_CONST). [def u32 x 42] emits OP_CONST with a jacl_u32() tagged value.
Typed global storage: [def i64 x 42] at global scope compiles RHS as raw i64, then emits OP_TO_DYN to box before OP_DEF_GLOBAL (globals always store tagged JaclVal)
Typed global read: $x where x is a typed global emits OP_GET_GLOBAL followed by conversion from dyn to the declared type (e.g. OP_TO_I64 with TYPE_DYN source)
Typed local read: $x where x is a typed i64 local just emits OP_GET_LOCAL (value is already raw on stack)
Compile error: [def i64 x "hello"] → 'type error: expected i64, got str'
Untyped [def x 42] continues to work unchanged (type is TYPE_DYN)
Type inference for untyped def: [def y $x] where x is i64 → y inferred as i64 (copy the type from the RHS expression)
Create test/jacl/typed_def_basic.jacl: def i64 x 42, print [to-string $x] => tests basic typed def works
Compiles cleanly with -Wall -Wextra -std=c99 -g
All existing tests pass (build.sh)
userStories.notes: The compiler needs a mechanism to thread 'expected type' through expression compilation. Add a JaclType expected_type field to the Compiler struct or pass it as a parameter to compiler__compile_node. When compiling literals, check expected_type to decide between tagged constant (OP_CONST) and typed constant (OP_CONST_I64/F64). Expression compilation should return a JaclType indicating the result type. For typed globals, the box/unbox on write/read is needed because the Environment table stores JaclVal. This is a pragmatic choice — optimization (typed global slots) can come later.

userStories.title: Typed mut and type-checked set!
userStories.description: As a JACL programmer, I want typed mutable bindings [mut TYPE name value] where set! enforces the declared type at compile time.
acceptanceCriteria: Compiler recognizes typed mut: [mut i64 counter 0] — same 3-arg pattern as typed def
Typed mut local: value compiled with expected_type context, cell created via OP_MAKE_CELL, type stored in Local.type
Typed mut global: value compiled with expected_type, boxed if needed (OP_TO_DYN), type stored in GlobalArity.type
set! type checking: [set! counter 10] where counter is i64 — literal 10 adopts i64 via contextual typing, compiles correctly
set! type error: [set! counter "hello"] where counter is i64 → compile error 'type error: cannot assign str to i64 binding counter'
set! dyn-to-typed error: [set! counter $y] where counter is i64 and y is dyn → compile error 'type error: cannot assign dyn to i64 binding counter'
set! typed-to-typed OK: [set! counter $y] where counter is i64 and y is i64 → compiles correctly
Type propagation through closure capture: mut i64 captured as upvalue retains i64 type in the Upvalue struct
Untyped [mut x 0] continues to work unchanged (type is TYPE_DYN, no type checking on set!)
Create test/jacl/typed_mut_basic.jacl: mut i64 x 0, set! x 42, print [to-string $x] => 42
Create test/jacl/typed_set_error.jacl with # expect-error: testing type mismatch on set!
Compiles cleanly with -Wall -Wextra -std=c99 -g
All existing tests pass (build.sh)
userStories.notes: set! already resolves local → upvalue → global from M10. The new work is: after resolving the target, check the target's declared type against the RHS expression's type. If both are concrete and different → compile error. If target is typed and RHS is dyn → compile error (must use [to TYPE $y] to convert). If target is dyn → no checking (existing behavior). The compiler already has the expected_type mechanism from US-006 — set! passes the target's type as expected_type when compiling the RHS.

userStories.title: Typed arithmetic — emit typed opcodes when operand types match
userStories.description: As a JACL programmer, I want arithmetic on typed values to compile to fast specialized opcodes and propagate result types through expressions.
acceptanceCriteria: When compiling [+ $a $b] where both a and b are i64: emit OP_ADD_I64 instead of OP_ADD
When compiling [* $a $b] where both are f64: emit OP_MUL_F64
When compiling [/ $a $b] where both are u64: emit OP_DIV_U64 (unsigned division)
When compiling [< $a $b] where both are u64: emit OP_LT_U64 (unsigned comparison)
When compiling [- $a] (unary negate) where a is i64: emit OP_NEG_I64
When both operands are i32 or both are f32: emit existing OP_ADD etc. (dynamic dispatch, already efficient)
When both operands are u32: emit existing OP_ADD etc. (u32 added to dynamic dispatch in US-005)
When both operands are dyn: emit existing OP_ADD etc. (fully backward compatible)
Type mismatch error: [+ $a $b] where a is i64 and b is f64 → compile error 'type error: cannot add i64 and f64'
Typed-dyn mismatch error: [+ $a $b] where a is i64 and b is dyn → compile error 'type error: cannot add i64 and dyn'
Contextual literal typing in arithmetic: [+ $a 1] where a is i64 → literal 1 compiled as i64 constant, emit OP_ADD_I64
Result type propagation: [+ $a $b] where both i64 → expression result type is i64
Nested expressions: [+ [* $a $b] $c] where all i64 → OP_MUL_I64 then OP_ADD_I64, result is i64
Type inference for untyped def: [def y [+ $a $b]] where a,b are i64 → y inferred as i64
Create test/jacl/typed_arithmetic.jacl: def i64 a 10; def i64 b 20; print [to-string [+ $a $b]] => 30
Create test/jacl/typed_arith_error.jacl with # expect-error: testing type mismatch in arithmetic
Compiles cleanly with -Wall -Wextra -std=c99 -g
All existing tests pass (build.sh)
userStories.notes: The key compiler change: in the arithmetic/comparison compilation section of compiler__compile_command, after compiling both operands, check their result types. If both are the same unboxed type (i64/u64/f64) → emit typed opcode. If both are the same boxed type (i32/u32/f32) → emit existing opcode. If both are dyn → emit existing opcode. If they differ → compile error. Contextual typing: when compiling the second operand, if the first operand's type is known and the second is a literal, pass the first's type as expected_type. The compiler__compile_node function should return a JaclType result — thread this through all expression compilation paths.

userStories.title: to builtin for explicit type conversions
userStories.description: As a JACL programmer, I want [to TYPE expr] to explicitly convert between types so I can bridge typed and dynamic code.
acceptanceCriteria: Compiler recognizes 'to' as a special form/builtin: exactly 2 arguments (type keyword + expression)
First argument must be a bare word matching a type keyword (i32, i64, u32, u64, f32, f64, dyn); compile error otherwise
Compiler compiles the expression (arg 2), then emits the appropriate OP_TO_* opcode with source type operand byte
[to i64 $x] where x is i32 → OP_TO_I64 with source TYPE_I32 (widen, sign-extend)
[to i64 $x] where x is u32 → OP_TO_I64 with source TYPE_U32 (widen, zero-extend)
[to i64 $x] where x is f64 → OP_TO_I64 with source TYPE_F64 (truncate to integer)
[to i64 $x] where x is dyn → OP_TO_I64 with source TYPE_DYN (runtime unbox and convert)
[to f64 $x] where x is i64 → OP_TO_F64 with source TYPE_I64 (integer to double)
[to dyn $x] where x is i64 → OP_TO_DYN with source TYPE_I64 (box into JACL_TAG_I64)
[to dyn $x] where x is dyn → no-op (skip emitting conversion)
[to i64 "hello"] → compile error 'type error: cannot convert str to i64'
Result type of [to TYPE expr] is always TYPE
Arity error: [to i64] or [to i64 $x $y] → compile error
Create test/jacl/type_conversions.jacl: def i32 n 42; def i64 big [to i64 $n]; print [to-string $big] => 42
Create test/jacl/to_error.jacl with # expect-error: testing invalid conversion
Compiles cleanly with -Wall -Wextra -std=c99 -g
All existing tests pass (build.sh)
userStories.notes: to is the bridge between typed and dynamic worlds. Key conversions: numeric widening (i32→i64, f32→f64), narrowing (i64→i32, truncates), int↔float, and boxing/unboxing (typed↔dyn). Invalid conversions (str↔numeric) are compile-time errors. The OP_TO_* opcodes read a source-type byte operand because the VM doesn't know the type of unboxed stack values. For dyn→typed conversions at runtime, the VM must examine the tagged value's actual tag and convert appropriately — runtime error if the value is not numeric.

userStories.title: Typed proc — optional return type and parameter types with call-site checking
userStories.description: As a JACL programmer, I want to annotate proc parameters and return types so that the compiler checks call sites and body expressions for type correctness.
acceptanceCriteria: Return type syntax: [proc TYPE name params body] — 4 args where first is type keyword. Disambiguation: 4 args + first is type keyword → has return type. 3 args → no return type (existing).
Compiler stores return type in a new field on the Compiler/FunctionState (e.g. JaclType return_type, default TYPE_DYN)
Parameter type syntax: type keywords interleaved in param list. [proc add [i64 a i64 b] { body }] — params a:i64, b:i64

Param list parsing: walk flat list of elements from the param AST_COMMAND (head + children). If current element is a type keyword and next element exists → consume (type, name) pair. Otherwise current element is untyped param name (TYPE_DYN).
Compiler stores parameter types in an array (e.g. JaclType param_types[MAX_PARAMS]) alongside the parameter names
Store param types and return type in GlobalArity/GlobalInfo so call sites can look them up
Mixed typed/untyped params: [proc f [i64 n str label x] { ... }] → n:i64, label:str, x:dyn
Variadic params: [proc f [i64 a & rest] { ... }] — rest is always dyn, & handled as before
Call-site checking: [add 1 2] where add expects [i64 a i64 b] → literals adopt i64 via contextual typing, compiles correctly
Call-site error: [add "x" 2] where add expects [i64 a i64 b] → compile error 'type error: argument 1 of add expected i64, got str'
Call-site dyn error: [add $x 2] where x is dyn and add expects i64 → compile error with suggestion to use [to i64 $x]

Return type checking: if return type declared, body's last expression type must match. [proc i64 bad [] { "hello" }] → compile error 'type error: proc bad declared return type i64, but body returns str'
Return type at call site: [def y [add 1 2]] where add returns i64 → y inferred as i64
Untyped procs unchanged: [proc f [a b] { body }] — all params dyn, return dyn
Create test/jacl/typed_proc.jacl: proc i64 add [i64 a i64 b] { [+ $a $b] }; print [to-string [add 3 4]] => 7
Create test/jacl/typed_proc_error.jacl with # expect-error: testing type mismatch at call site
Compiles cleanly with -Wall -Wextra -std=c99 -g
All existing tests pass (build.sh)
userStories.notes: Param type parsing walks the flat list from the param AST_COMMAND. The head and all children form a flat sequence. For each element: check if it's a bare word matching a type keyword (via is_type_keyword). If yes and next exists → typed param. If no → untyped param. The & for variadic is handled as before — skip it, next element is rest name (always dyn). Store param types alongside arity info in GlobalArity so compiler__resolve_global_arity can return them for call-site checking. Return type checking: the compiler knows the body's result type from the last compiled expression — compare with declared return type.

userStories.title: Update print and to-string for new numeric types
userStories.description: As a JACL programmer, I want print and to-string to correctly display values of all new numeric types.
acceptanceCriteria: OP_PRINT handles JACL_TAG_U32: prints unsigned integer (e.g. 255)
OP_PRINT handles JACL_TAG_I64: extracts int64_t from heap, prints (e.g. 42)
OP_PRINT handles JACL_TAG_U64: extracts uint64_t from heap, prints (e.g. 999)
OP_PRINT handles JACL_TAG_F64: extracts double from heap, prints (e.g. 3.14)
vm__fmt_value handles all 4 new tags for recursive formatting (used by to-string and container formatting)
OP_TO_STRING handles all 4 new tags
Typed (unboxed) values: when printing a typed i64/u64/f64 local, the compiler emits OP_TO_DYN before OP_PRINT to box the value first (print always operates on tagged JaclVal)
String interpolation works with new types: "x is $x" where x is a boxed i64 → correct string
No regression on existing print behavior for i32, f32, strings, vectors, maps, etc.
Create test/jacl/print_typed.jacl: def i64 x 42; print [to-string $x] (testing basic print of typed values via to-string since direct print of unboxed values requires OP_TO_DYN)
Compiles cleanly with -Wall -Wextra -std=c99 -g
All existing tests pass (build.sh)
userStories.notes: Print always operates on tagged JaclVal. For typed (unboxed) values on the stack, the compiler must emit OP_TO_DYN before OP_PRINT to box them. This means the print path in the compiler needs to check the expression's type: if unboxed, emit conversion first. The vm__fmt_value function already has a switch on type tags — add cases for U32, I64, U64, F64. Use PRIi64/PRIu64 format specifiers for 64-bit types. F64 formatting should match existing f32 formatting style.

userStories.title: Comprehensive M11 integration tests
userStories.description: As a developer, I want comprehensive tests covering all type system features to ensure correctness and prevent regressions.
acceptanceCriteria: Create test/test_m11.c with integration tests using test_helpers.h pattern (run_ok/run_err helpers, PrintCapture buffer)
Tests cover: value representation — u32, i64, u64, f64 constructors, accessors, predicates (unit-level)
Tests cover: typed def for all numeric types — i32, i64, u32, u64, f32, f64
Tests cover: typed mut and set! with type enforcement
Tests cover: typed arithmetic — i64+i64, f64*f64, u64/u64 producing correct results
Tests cover: compile errors for type mismatches (def, set!, arithmetic, proc calls)
Tests cover: to builtin — conversions between all numeric type pairs
Tests cover: typed proc — return type checking, param type checking, call-site checking
Tests cover: contextual typing — literals adopting expected types in typed contexts
Tests cover: type inference — untyped def infers type from typed RHS expression
Tests cover: nested typed expressions — [+ [* $a $b] $c] all i64
Tests cover: typed closures — typed params in closures, typed upvalue capture
Tests cover: print/to-string for all new types
Tests cover: interaction with existing features — typed values in error handling (try), typed values passed to collections (auto-box to dyn)
Add test/test_m11.c to build.sh TESTS array
All existing M1-M10 tests still pass (no regressions)
Compiles cleanly with -Wall -Wextra -std=c99 -g
All tests pass (build.sh)
userStories.notes: Follow the same test_m10.c pattern: PrintCapture(4096), run_ok/run_err helpers, TestEntry table grouped by US-XXX comments. run_err tests should cover both compile-time type errors and runtime errors (e.g. to dyn→i64 conversion of non-numeric value). Test edge cases: overflow on narrow (i64→i32), division by zero in typed ops, max/min values for each type.
